rows.title: Drupal site takeover vulnerability exploited in attacks
rows.summary: The Drupal security team warns that a second critical flaw is actively being exploited in the wild to breach unpatched websites. Administrators should apply the latest security updates immediately.
rows.action: Update Drupal to the latest security release.

rows.title: CISA warns of exploited N-able bug as company restores email platform
rows.summary: CISA warned that a vulnerability in N-able's email security platform has been exploited in the wild. The company is restoring the platform and urges agencies to apply the patch before Thanksgiving.
rows.action: Apply the available patch for the N-able vulnerability as soon as possible

rows.title: GL.iNet Routers, KVMs Compromised via Remote Management Service Flaw
rows.summary: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in the GoodCloud remote management service to install malware on GL.iNet routers and KVM devices. Remediation requires flashing new firmware to the affected hardware.
rows.action: Flash affected devices with the new firmware provided by GL.iNet

rows.title: CVE-2026-124251: WPIDE Nonce Bypass Leading to RCE
rows.summary: WPIDE versions up to 3.6.4 contain a CSRF nonce bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote code execution. A security service validates the nonce only under specific parameter conditions, leaving administrative endpoints exposed.
rows.action: Update WPIDE once a patched version is available or disable the plugin.

rows.title: OpenJDK Java4Shell vulnerability allows remote code execution
rows.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability in OpenJDK affects multiple enterprise applications including Jenkins, Jira, and Confluence. Unauthenticated attackers can exploit the flaw to execute arbitrary code.
rows.action: Check for vendor advisories and updates for OpenJDK and dependent enterprise applications.

rows.title: New Windows SignDrop zero‑day gives hackers SYSTEM privileges
rows.summary: A new Windows zero‑day, named SignDrop, was disclosed that allows attackers to obtain SYSTEM privileges through a signature‑validation flaw. The vulnerability is unpatched and rated critical.
rows.action: Monitor for signs of SignDrop exploitation and apply mitigations.

rows.title: LNbits Urges Shutdown of Bitcoin Lightning Wallet Servers Due to Attacks
rows.summary: LNbits urged operators to shut down their Bitcoin Lightning wallet servers immediately following a wave of active exploitation. An attacker used an exploit on new accounts to steal funds before patches could be released.
rows.action: Shut down LNbits servers immediately until security fixes are released.

rows.title: QNAP warns of Plex2Shell attacks exploiting Plex Media Server on NAS devices
rows.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a vulnerability chain dubbed Plex2Shell to compromise QNAP network-attached storage devices. QNAP has urged users to update their Plex Media Server installations immediately.
rows.action: Update Plex Media Server to the latest version available in the QNAP App Center.

rows.title: SonicWall warns of unpatched security flaws in end-of-life GMS software
rows.summary: SonicWall issued a warning regarding two security vulnerabilities impacting end-of-life Global Management System products. The vendor confirmed that these vulnerabilities will not receive software patches.
rows.action: Upgrade from end-of-life GMS systems to supported alternatives.

rows.title: CVE-2026-81648: Unpatched CryptoPayment Gateway Flaw Targeted
rows.summary: Threat actors are attempting to exploit an unpatched maximum-severity vulnerability in the CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin. The flaw permits unauthenticated users to delete arbitrary files and extract credentials.
rows.action: Disable the vulnerable plugin until a patch becomes available.

rows.title: PHP2Shell Attacks Target Palo Alto Firewalls
rows.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting critical PHP vulnerabilities known as PHP2Shell to target Palo Alto firewalls. Millions of instances remain potentially exposed following more than a week of active attacks.
rows.action: Apply available security patches or mitigation measures immediately.

rows.title: CISA warns of exploited Fragnesia Linux privilege escalation flaw
rows.summary: CISA issued a warning regarding a high-severity Linux kernel privilege escalation vulnerability being actively chained in the wild with PHP2Shell flaws. Federal agencies have been instructed to apply patches.
rows.action: Patch the affected Linux kernel components as advised by CISA.

rows.title: Critical RCE Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
rows.summary: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway contain critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities that are actively exploited in the wild. Administrators must update affected software and perform a compromise assessment.
rows.action: Update affected Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway software and run a compromise assessment.

rows.title: CVE-2026-103406: HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Router OS Command Injection Vulnerability
rows.summary: A remote OS command injection vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑103406) was found in HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root. Exploitation in the wild has been confirmed, and CISA advises applying vendor mitigations and updates.
rows.action: Apply vendor‑provided mitigations and updates as instructed

rows.title: CVE-2026-133275: Mitel MiCollab Arbitrary File Upload Vulnerability
rows.summary: Mitel MiCollab contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in its AWV component due to insufficient validation, allowing unauthenticated attackers to upload arbitrary files. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog after confirming active exploitation.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-133323: Mitel MiCollab OS Command Injection Vulnerability
rows.summary: Mitel MiCollab contains an OS command injection vulnerability in its AWV component that enables unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary system commands. CISA added the issue to its KEV catalog following confirmed active exploitation.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-133469: Vates Xen Orchestra Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
rows.summary: Vates Xen Orchestra contains an input validation flaw that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication and execute administrative actions using a crafted token. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog following confirmed active exploitation.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-133324: Mitel MiCollab Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
rows.summary: Mitel MiCollab contains a failure to secure authentication controls in its AWV component, allowing unauthenticated attackers to perform unauthorized actions. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog due to confirmed exploitation.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-133311: Mitel MiCollab Weak Authentication Vulnerability
rows.summary: Mitel MiCollab contains a weak authentication flaw in its AWV component that allows unauthenticated attackers to access sensitive information using predictable identifiers. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog after confirming exploitation.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-133303: Mitel MiCollab AWV XML Injection Vulnerability
rows.summary: Mitel MiCollab contains an XML injection vulnerability in its Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing component allowing unauthenticated command execution. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-131914: Idunno.AntiCsrf RCE Vulnerability Exploit
rows.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability affects the legacy ASP.NET anti-CSRF library Idunno.AntiCsrf. Researchers report active exploitation in the wild against the unpatched library.
rows.action: Discontinue using the vulnerable Idunno.AntiCsrf library.

rows.title: Unpatched Danfoss Refrigeration Controller Flaws Allow Remote Takeover
rows.summary: Six unpatched vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers allow unauthenticated remote attackers to take over the devices. Government cybersecurity agencies have advised operators of the risk as no patch currently exists.
rows.action: Review network exposure and follow guidance from national cybersecurity agencies.

rows.title: CVE-2026-134624: N-able MailAssure Server-Side Request Forgery
rows.summary: N-able MailAssure contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the LDAP synchronization connection check. Exploitation in the wild has been confirmed by CISA.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions.

rows.title: AI agents discover zero‑day in MONAI Label allowing unauthenticated file write and root access
rows.summary: Attackers using autonomous AI agents identified a previously unknown vulnerability in the MONAI Label medical‑imaging server that permits unauthenticated file‑write outside its storage directory. The flaw was exploited to gain root access on a university server; no patch is currently available.
rows.action: Add detection for the Cairn tool targeting medical imaging applications.

rows.title: Hackers Exploit Cisco Expressway Vulnerability Soon After PoC Release
rows.summary: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Cisco Expressway after a proof‑of‑concept was released, compromising a clustered deployment at a Russian organization. They used the access to set up tooling for lateral movement within the network.
rows.action: Review and apply any available Cisco Expressway patches addressing the database service RCE.

rows.title: Java4Shell Exploitation Attempts Begin as Vendors Rush Out Advisories
rows.summary: Security firms report probing and exploit attempts targeting Java4Shell, prompting vendors like Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat, and Siemens to issue advisories. Affected organisations must apply available patches and monitor perimeter telemetry.
rows.action: Review vendor advisories and apply available patches immediately.

rows.title: CVE-2026-90817: Vanderbilt University REDCap Code Injection Vulnerability
rows.summary: Vanderbilt University REDCap contains a code injection vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code via crafted HTTP requests. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions.

rows.title: CVE-2024-10441: Synology DSM and BeeStation OS Output Escaping Vulnerability
rows.summary: Synology DiskStation Manager and BeeStation OS contain an improper encoding vulnerability in the system plugin daemon allowing arbitrary code execution. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions.

rows.title: CVE-2026-40217: LiteLLM sandbox escape in custom-code guardrail
rows.summary: LiteLLM contains a sandbox escape vulnerability in its custom-code guardrail endpoint allowing arbitrary code execution. The issue was patched in version 1.83.11 by replacing the hand-rolled sandbox with RestrictedPython.

rows.title: CVE-2026-114713: UnrealIRCd improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability
rows.summary: UnrealIRCd contains an improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability allowing network users to inject server-to-server commands executed with server authority. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following confirmation of active attacks.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: Google Chrome Exploited Use-After-Free Vulnerability in XML
rows.summary: An anonymous report disclosed a high-severity use-after-free flaw in Google Chrome's XML component. The vulnerability is currently being exploited in active attacks in the wild.
rows.action: Update Google Chrome to the latest version immediately.

rows.title: CVE-2026-20320: Cisco BroadWorks XXE Vulnerability
rows.summary: An improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability in Cisco BroadWorks allows unauthenticated attackers to read sensitive configuration information. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild and added the flaw to its KEV catalog.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-111560: Barracuda Networks Multiple Products OS Command Injection
rows.summary: An OS command injection vulnerability in multiple Barracuda Networks products allows authenticated administrators to execute root commands via a crafted timezone value. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild and added the flaw to its KEV catalog.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-111793: Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder Resource Transfer Flaw
rows.summary: An incorrect resource transfer between spheres vulnerability in Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder allows authenticated users to process unintended document types. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild and added the flaw to its KEV catalog.
products: Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-123218: IBM Aspera Faspex Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability
rows.summary: IBM Aspera Faspex contains an incorrect authorization flaw allowing authenticated users to craft specific messages and escalate privileges. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog following confirmation of active exploitation.
rows.action: Apply mitigations or updates in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-102895: GPUStack Improper Authentication Vulnerability
rows.summary: GPUStack contains an improper authentication vulnerability enabling unauthenticated administrative access and code execution. The flaw has been added to CISA's KEV catalog following confirmed exploitation in the wild.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-116779: SignalWire FreeSwitch Code Injection Vulnerability
rows.summary: SignalWire FreeSwitch contains a code injection vulnerability allowing configuration disclosure and arbitrary command execution. The issue is actively exploited in the wild and has been added to CISA's KEV catalog.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 guidance.

rows.title: Brotli Decoder Out-of-Bounds Write Triggers Multi-Platform Patching
rows.summary: An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Google's Brotli decoder affects multiple runtimes including Node.js and Python packages. Vendors are issuing updates to address potential code execution risks.
rows.action: Update PHP Windows packages to the latest patched releases.

rows.title: CVE-2026-41709: Broadcom VMware ESX Insufficient Logging Vulnerability
rows.summary: Broadcom VMware ESX contains an insufficient logging vulnerability allowing administrators to perform operations without logging. Exploitation in the wild is confirmed by CISA.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-46300: Linux Kernel Missing Variable Initialization Vulnerability
rows.summary: The Linux Kernel contains a variable initialization flaw that causes ESP input processing to decrypt shared fragments in place, allowing for unintended page-cache data modification. CISA added this vulnerability to its KEV catalog following confirmed exploitation.
rows.action: Apply mitigations according to vendor instructions.

rows.title: Compromise of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
rows.summary: Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were found to be critically broken due to key generation ceremony errors. Attackers can brute-force acquire these private keys within seconds.
rows.action: Apply the out-of-band Windows updates to remove trust in affected eMudhra certificates.

rows.title: Hex.pm RCE Flaw Exploited to Compromise Six Production Servers
rows.summary: Attackers exploited a remote code execution vulnerability on Hex.pm affecting six production servers. The maintainers patched all affected servers shortly after the initial malicious request.
rows.action: Ensure all Hex.pm registry server deployments are running the latest patched build.

rows.title: CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243: GeoServer Flaws Exploited
rows.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting two security flaws in GeoServer, including an arbitrary file read vulnerability. WatchTowr warned of unauthenticated remote code execution chains resulting from these issues.
rows.action: Update GeoServer to the latest patched version immediately.

rows.title: Drupal patches critical remote code execution vulnerability
rows.summary: The Drupal Security Team patched a critical remote code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to take over vulnerable sites. Administrators should apply the latest security updates immediately.
rows.action: Apply the updated security release immediately to address the remaining installer gap.

rows.title: Palo Alto Networks Patches Fragnesia Flaw Used in Attacks
rows.summary: A threat group chained vulnerabilities in AI-assisted attacks affecting multiple servers. Palo Alto Networks released patches to address the issue.
rows.action: Update Palo Alto Networks firewalls to the latest patched version.

rows.title: VMware vCenter Hit by Another Critical 9.8-Rated Auth Bypass Flaw After Zero-Day Exploitation
rows.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑123903) in VMware vCenter’s Directory Service was rated 9.8 CVSS and has been exploited in the wild. Broadcom released patches for the flaw across VMware products.
rows.action: Apply the Broadcom patches to all affected VMware products immediately

rows.title: Azure API Management Flaw Exploited to Target Norwegian Energy Firms
rows.summary: Microsoft patched an Azure API Management vulnerability that was actively exploited to compromise secrets at Norwegian energy companies and other sectors. The vendor closed the security gap after observing targeted attacks.
rows.action: Notify customers to apply the Azure API Management patch if not already done.

rows.title: Critical VMware vCenter Flaw Allows Network Attackers to Bypass Authentication
rows.summary: VMware disclosed a critical vulnerability in vCenter that allows network‑connected attackers to bypass authentication and gain full control. The vendor released patches for all supported branches, with no workaround available.
rows.action: Apply the latest VMware patches to affected ESX hosts

rows.title: WHMCS SQL Injection Flaw Exposes Customer Data and Admin Password Hashes
rows.summary: An unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in WHMCS allows attackers to retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes. The vendor disclosed the flaw and released patches.
rows.action: Update to the latest patched version of WHMCS immediately.

rows.title: CVE-2026-123007: Critical vulnerabilities in NGINX allow remote code execution
rows.summary: F5 disclosed five vulnerabilities in NGINX enabling unauthenticated remote attackers to execute code with worker process privileges. While researchers demonstrated CVE-2026-123007, no active in-the-wild exploitation has been reported.
rows.action: Update NGINX to the latest patched version immediately, prioritizing internet-facing appliances.

rows.title: CVE-2026-134814: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions
rows.summary: A critical code injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-134814) was found in binary-parser versions before 2.3.1, allowing attackers controlling parser definitions to execute arbitrary JavaScript. The flaw has a CVSS score of 9.2 and is mitigated by upgrading to version 2.3.1 or later.
rows.action: Upgrade binary-parser to version 2.3.1 or later.

rows.title: CVE-2026-126714: Critical Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in PHP
rows.summary: A critical vulnerability in PHP allows remote code execution affecting various downstream vendor products. The PHP Foundation released security updates to address the flaw.
rows.action: Update PHP to the latest patched version provided by the vendor.

rows.title: Ghostscript Sandbox-Escape RCE Discovered in File Processing
rows.summary: A vulnerability in Ghostscript permits crafted files to break out of the security sandbox and achieve remote code execution. Security researchers demonstrated the flaw affecting servers that process uploaded PDF and image documents.
rows.action: Update Ghostscript to the latest patched version.

rows.title: Apache warns of Roller RCE vulnerability exploited in attacks
rows.summary: Apache released security updates addressing a critical remote code execution flaw in Roller. Threat actors are actively exploiting this vulnerability in the wild.
rows.action: Update Apache Roller to the latest patched version immediately.

rows.title: Critical memory bug in GPGME (CVE‑2026‑129975) allows data theft via crafted OpenPGP keys
rows.summary: A critical memory corruption vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑129975) in the GPGME library can be triggered by a malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID, potentially allowing attackers to read application data. The GnuPG project released patched versions fixing the issue, affecting all software using GPGME prior to version 2.3.0.
rows.action: Upgrade to GPGME 2.3.0 or later

rows.title: CVE-2025-42884: SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal Improper Neutralization Vulnerability
rows.summary: SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal contains an improper neutralization flaw in data query logic allowing unauthenticated server information disclosure or modification. CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following confirmation of active exploitation.
rows.action: Apply vendor mitigations and updates in accordance with CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-23871: WhatsApp Patches Flaw Suspected of In-The-Wild Abuse
rows.summary: Meta patched a security vulnerability in WhatsApp for Android that may have been exploited in scam messages. The issue involves incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs.
rows.action: Update WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business to version 2.26.17.4 or later.

rows.title: CVE-2026-99312: Linux KVM Flaw Allows Guest VMs Access to Host Memory
rows.summary: A vulnerability in Linux KVM on AMD hosts allows guest virtual machines to access host memory and potentially other customers' virtual machines. Fixed kernels have been released.
rows.action: Update the Linux kernel to the latest patched version.

rows.title: F5 BIG-IP Critical Vulnerabilities Allow Traffic Disruption and Potential RCE
rows.summary: F5 disclosed six critical vulnerabilities in BIG-IP that let unauthenticated attackers crash the Traffic Management Microkernel or potentially achieve remote code execution in specific setups. The flaws require targeted configurations involving iRules or APM policies to trigger.
rows.action: Apply the emergency patches released by F5 for BIG-IP vulnerabilities.

rows.title: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: PHP flaws exploited in the wild
rows.summary: Critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are being actively exploited in the wild. Palo Alto Networks issued an advisory regarding the impact on their products.
rows.action: Upgrade PHP installations to version 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35 or later immediately.

rows.title: ASUS warns of critical hard-coded key flaw in Control Center Express
rows.summary: ASUS patched three critical vulnerabilities in Control Center Express that could allow remote administrative control. Users are advised to update to version 1.7.29.
rows.action: Update to Control Center Express version 1.7.29.

rows.title: Critical memory corruption vulnerability disclosed in Java
rows.summary: Oracle released a patch for a critical memory corruption vulnerability in Java that could allow attackers to gain server control. Researchers used AI to assist in discovering the flaw.
rows.action: Identify affected Java installations and immediately patch the Oracle Java vulnerability CVE-2026-114938.

rows.title: CVE-2026-115560: PHP Critical Security Release Advisory
rows.summary: PHP published an emergency security release regarding CVE-2026-115560. Technical details and fixed versions are currently developing.
rows.action: Assess whether the NSA incident indicates any unmet issues in the PHP patches and verify patch integrity.

rows.title: Tor 0.4.9.17 Released to Mitigate Ongoing Relay Denial-of-Service Attacks
rows.summary: The Tor Project released version 0.4.9.17 to address several security issues affecting built-in denial-of-service protections. The update responds to ongoing DoS attacks targeting Tor network relays.
rows.action: Upgrade Tor relay and node installations to version 0.4.9.17 or later.

rows.title: Apple Audio Service Flaw Allowed Unauthorized Microphone Recording
rows.summary: A patched vulnerability in Apple's audio service allowed iOS and iPadOS applications to record audio despite users explicitly denying microphone permissions. Apple released security updates addressing the flaw, and researchers confirmed no evidence of active exploitation.
rows.action: Update Apple devices to the latest available software version.

rows.title: Rspamd 4.3.0 fixes denial of service and authentication bypass bugs
rows.summary: Rspamd version 4.3.0 addresses multiple bugs allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash spam filter workers or forge authentication results. The update includes fixes for HTTP request handling and milter proxy issues.
rows.action: Update to Rspamd 4.3.0 to resolve worker crash and authentication bugs.

rows.title: CVE-2026-99362: Linux kernel NFS server flaw lets attackers gain root
rows.summary: A long-standing vulnerability in the Linux kernel Network File System server allows remote attackers to obtain root privileges. An update or patch should be applied to secure affected systems.
rows.action: Check vendor advisories and apply available patches for the Linux kernel NFS server.

rows.title: Elecbrakes Bluetooth Controllers Vulnerable to Forced Braking
rows.summary: Elecbrakes Bluetooth controllers contain critical flaws that allow nearby attackers to force a trailer’s brakes, creating a risk of accidents. No fix has been released yet, and users are advised to disable Bluetooth and await a vendor patch.
rows.action: Disable Bluetooth on the controllers and apply patches when released

rows.title: phpAfterShell Session Overwrite Deserialization Vulnerability
rows.summary: An interrupted session overwrite operation in phpAfterShell allows attackers controlling fresh data to trigger deserialization and remote code execution. Security researchers disclosed the flaw and recommended applying available vendor updates.
rows.action: Check vendor advisories for updates and patch phpAfterShell immediately.

rows.title: CISA KEV Adds Exploited Flaws in LiteLLM, Synology, Axis, and REDCap
rows.summary: CISA added four vulnerabilities affecting LiteLLM, Synology DiskStation Manager, Apache Axis, and REDCap to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The additions follow evidence of active exploitation in the wild.
rows.action: Apply vendor patches or mitigations listed in the CISA KEV catalog.

rows.title: CVE-2026-115731: Perforce Puppet Enterprise Deserialization Flaw
rows.summary: Perforce Puppet Enterprise contains a deserialization flaw allowing authenticated agents or attackers with a valid certificate to execute arbitrary code. CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
rows.action: Apply the updates provided by the vendor.

rows.title: CVE-2026-90436: Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection Vulnerability
rows.summary: Apache Axis contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via SOAP fault messages. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild.
rows.action: Discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

rows.title: Multiple vulnerabilities discovered in Dixell refrigeration units
rows.summary: VulnCheck disclosed 14 vulnerabilities in Dixell refrigeration units providing attackers with root access. Online honeypots have observed active probing and exploitation attempts against these devices.

rows.title: NoisyTCP vulnerability in Linux kernel allows server crashes
rows.summary: An 11-year-old vulnerability known as NoisyTCP impacts nearly all Linux distributions. Attackers can exploit it to crash Linux servers running services like Nginx, Apache, and SSH with default configurations.
rows.action: Apply available kernel updates from Linux distributions as they become available.

rows.title: Flight Centre Travel Group Discloses Customer Data Breach
rows.summary: Flight Centre Travel Group reported unauthorized access to a third-party accommodation booking system. The incident exposed customer names, and in some cases, passport and health details.
rows.action: Review booking system logs and monitor accounts for potential misuse.

rows.title: Colorado cyberattack disables myColorado app and steals data of 150,000 users
rows.summary: A cyberattack disabled Colorado’s myColorado app and resulted in the theft of personal data belonging to approximately 150,000 users. The state warned that the stolen information could be used for identity fraud.
rows.action: Investigate the breach and notify affected users

rows.title: Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Attacks on Critical Infrastructure
rows.summary: Attackers using AI agents breached computer systems at Swiss critical infrastructure operators in confirmed intrusions. The incidents resulted in no major operational disruptions and victims remain unnamed.

rows.title: SAP Confirms Cyberattack Involving Stolen Employee Tokens on GitHub
rows.summary: SAP identified unauthorized activity on GitHub where attackers utilized stolen employee tokens. The intruders reportedly accessed and modified source code repositories.
rows.action: Revoke and rotate any compromised employee tokens and audit GitHub access logs.

rows.title: FIFA hacked, cybercriminals claim access to sensitive internal records
rows.summary: Cybercriminals breached FIFA's internal systems, gaining access to limited personal and business data. FIFA confirmed the intrusion and is investigating with law enforcement.

rows.title: Japan Education Ministry Discloses Government Procurement System Breach
rows.summary: Hackers breached Japan's education ministry government procurement system, potentially exposing business records and email addresses. The ministry disclosed the incident earlier this week.

rows.title: 1Password customer data stolen after employee GitHub account breach
rows.summary: 1Password disclosed a data breach resulting from a compromised employee GitHub account used to deploy malicious code. Customer data was stolen during the incident.

rows.title: Volant Manticore Iranian Threat Group Targets Cypriot Organizations
rows.summary: An undocumented Iranian threat group named Volant Manticore is targeting organizations in Cyprus for intelligence gathering. The campaign highlights ongoing regional espionage activities by state-sponsored actors.

rows.title: SYS010 malware abuses browser management to spy on Gmail, Outlook
rows.summary: A new version of the SYS01 infostealer delivered via Meta ads abuses browser management to install data-stealing extensions. The campaign targets user email accounts like Gmail and Outlook.

rows.title: Keenadu and Triada malware preinstalled on over 220,000 Android devices
rows.summary: Kaspersky reported that preinstalled malware families Keenadu and Triada infected over 220,000 Android devices in the first ten months of 2026. The malicious software is embedded directly within device firmware prior to user purchase.

rows.title: Remus Malware Steals Gmail Messages via Fake Google Sheets Extension
rows.summary: The Remus infostealer deploys a malicious browser extension to extract Gmail messages from targeted users. The operators marketed this capability as a zero-day exploit against Google's email service.

rows.title: GoodGuys campaign uses fake expert interviews to steal Google logins
rows.summary: An ongoing phishing campaign named GoodGuys impersonates major brands to distribute fake interview invitations that steal corporate credentials. Affected organizations should be on alert for fraudulent interview lures.
rows.action: Warn employees to be vigilant against unsolicited expert interview invitations requesting credential logins.

rows.title: FinCEN takes systems offline following cybersecurity incident
rows.summary: The US Treasury Department took multiple systems offline following unauthorized access to a limited subset of networks. Officials are investigating the incident.

rows.title: FIFA discloses cyberattack resulting in access to personal and business data
rows.summary: FIFA announced that unauthorized actors accessed a limited set of personal and business information during a recent cyberattack. The organization is currently working with law enforcement and relevant authorities to investigate the breach.

rows.title: Ransomware Attack Disrupts Operations at University Hospital of Guadeloupe
rows.summary: A suspected ransomware attack impaired computer systems at the University Hospital of Guadeloupe. The incident forced medical staff to postpone surgeries, suspend cancer treatments, and revert to manual operations.
products: University Hospital of Guadeloupe computer systems

rows.title: Com-Affiliated Hackers Target Cloud Accounts via Vishing for Extortion
rows.summary: Threat actors linked to Com have conducted multiple waves of vishing attacks since August 2026 to compromise cloud accounts. The campaign resulted in data theft and extortion attempts against financial, healthcare, and legal organizations.
rows.action: Monitor cloud access logs for anomalous authentication activity and reinforce phishing-resistant MFA.

rows.title: Check Point Security Management Servers Hacked in AI‑Assisted Campaign
rows.summary: Threat actors compromised Check Point Security Management Servers as part of a campaign that leveraged AI tools. The attacks originated from 99 IP addresses and affected organizations across multiple industries.
rows.action: Investigate the breach and apply any available patches or mitigations

rows.title: Inception extortion gang launches large‑scale vishing campaign against SSO credentials
rows.summary: The newly identified extortion group Inception launched a large‑scale vishing campaign targeting SSO credentials of numerous global brands. Victims are being pressured to pay to avoid credential misuse.
rows.action: Update threat intel to include possible ShinyHunters involvement

rows.title: Threat actors use agentic AI framework ARTEX to abuse exposed secrets
rows.summary: Threat actors utilized the agentic offensive security framework ARTEX to scan GitHub for OAuth secrets. The compromised credentials were then used to execute authenticated actions within targeted organization tenants.
rows.action: Add the newly identified actor groups to threat intel tracking for ARTEX.

rows.title: McDonald’s Japan breach exposes customer purchase and location data
rows.summary: McDonald’s Japan disclosed a cybersecurity breach that exposed customers’ purchase histories and mobile device location data. The incident affects the personal information of many customers and may require notification and remediation.
rows.action: Investigate the breach, secure systems, and notify affected customers

rows.title: Carnegie Endowment donor data leaked after third‑party vendor breach
rows.summary: A cyberattack on the third‑party vendor Soapbox Engage exposed personal information of donors to the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. The breach resulted in the leakage of donor names, contact details, and donation amounts.

rows.title: European Commission confirms data theft in EU Academy breach
rows.summary: The European Commission confirmed that attackers breached its EU Academy online learning platform and stole personal data of an undisclosed number of users. The breach has prompted investigations and notifications to affected individuals.

rows.title: Radware Discloses Breach Exposing Customer Cloud Access Keys
rows.summary: Radware suffered a data breach after attackers gained access to customer account details and cloud access keys via an unsecured internal Cloud WAF management API. The exposed API allowed unauthorized external access to sensitive customer assets.

rows.title: GlobeTopper suffers $2.5M loss after hackers steal $70k in gift cards
rows.summary: Hackers breached the B2B top‑up solutions provider GlobeTopper, redeeming digital gift cards worth $70,000. The attack disrupted operations and caused an estimated $2.5 million in lost revenue.
rows.action: Investigate the incident, revoke compromised gift cards, and strengthen authentication controls.

rows.title: Spanish LaLiga confirms hackers stole soccer fans’ personal data
rows.summary: LaLiga announced that hackers accessed and stole personal data of fans and affiliated club users. The breach exposed names, contact details and other identifying information.

rows.title: Volant Manticore deploys IPFS-based KuboShell backdoor in espionage campaigns
rows.summary: The Iran‑aligned group Volant Manticore has been observed using a custom backdoor called KuboShell that leverages IPFS for command‑and‑control and deploys the Homa post‑compromise framework. The campaign has targeted telecom operators, airlines and critical infrastructure in Cyprus.
rows.action: Detect and remove KuboShell implants and block IPFS traffic used for C2

rows.title: Turnitin discloses cyberattack affecting customer‑facing systems
rows.summary: Turnitin announced that unauthorized activity was detected on some of its customer‑facing systems. The company is investigating the breach and assessing potential impact on user data.
rows.action: Investigate the intrusion and secure affected systems

rows.title: Unclassified intel system hit by hackers affecting CIA and ODNI
rows.summary: Hackers breached an unclassified intelligence system affecting the CIA and ODNI. Sources confirmed the incident while stating no other systems are currently at risk.

rows.title: Korea Electric Power Corporation confirms data breach impacting 1.5 million
rows.summary: Korea Electric Power Corporation confirmed that a threat actor breached its internal network and accessed systems holding customer and employee records. The incident impacted approximately 1.5 million individuals.

rows.title: FBI National Crime Information Center breached in second incident
rows.summary: FBI systems containing the National Crime Information Center database were breached by attackers. The incident marks the second time the agency has been compromised within two months.

rows.title: Rackspace Spot breach exposes customer Kubernetes secrets
rows.summary: Hackers breached the Rackspace Spot cloud platform using compromised credentials to deploy unauthorized workloads and access customer Kubernetes secrets. Rackspace notified affected customers about the security incident.
rows.action: Migrate services and download data from the Rackspace Spot platform before the December 8 deadline.

rows.title: European Commission confirms AI-assisted cyberattack disrupted systems
rows.summary: The European Commission confirmed it suffered a cyberattack utilizing a publicly available AI tool, forcing several internal applications offline. Officials acknowledged the incident during a press briefing following initial reporting.
rows.action: Notify affected EU Academy users and assess data exposure.

rows.title: Bromcom data breach exposes 355,051 accounts
rows.summary: UK education software provider Bromcom suffered a data breach involving a legacy single sign-on registration system. The incident exposed over 355,000 email addresses belonging to staff and pupils at UK schools.

rows.title: GoFundMe donor information exposed in data breach
rows.summary: GoFundMe reported that donor personal information was exposed in a data breach. The incident affects donor records and may lead to privacy risks.

rows.title: Cleverbridge data breach exposes customers' credit card numbers and CVVs
rows.summary: Hackers breached the Cleverbridge e‑commerce platform and stole customers' payment card numbers and CVV codes. The breach was disclosed on 2026‑11‑22, prompting the company to warn affected users and begin investigation.
rows.action: Notify affected customers and reset compromised payment credentials

rows.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health vulnerability exploited to steal tenant data
rows.summary: Microsoft reported that attackers exploited a flaw in its Entra Connect Health service to obtain administrator email addresses and tenant configuration details, resulting in a data breach. The company is urging affected organizations to review and secure their environments.
rows.action: Review and secure Entra Connect Health configurations and rotate compromised credentials

rows.title: AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Target Indian Banks and Fintech Firms for Unauthorized Payments
rows.summary: Threat actors utilized AI-assisted cyberattacks to target banking and financial entities in India. The campaign resulted in unauthorized financial transactions and impacted technology service providers.

rows.title: Austrian Foreign Ministry website breached, contact details accessed
rows.summary: Hackers breached an Austrian Foreign Ministry website to access official contact details of employees and diplomats. The ministry reported the incident after discovering unauthorized access to staff information.

rows.title: OpenRouter Drops Providers Following Months of Prompt Theft
rows.summary: Attackers surreptitiously stole user data from three AI inference providers over several months without the companies realizing. The incident exposed zero-data-retention requests, prompting OpenRouter to drop the affected hosting partners.
rows.action: Review API endpoints and rotate keys associated with affected providers.

rows.title: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers and KVM devices
rows.summary: Hackers exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet cloud remote management services to install custom malware, including backdoors and reverse shells on customer devices. The vendor confirmed the attacks and ongoing exploitation.

rows.title: BADBOX 3.0 Botnet Returns with Large-Scale Android Ad-Fraud Operations
rows.summary: The BADBOX malware campaign has returned across generic Android TV boxes to conduct large-scale ad fraud. The botnet generates billions of daily requests following previous disruptions.

rows.title: N-able Suffers Service Disruption Due to Cyberattack
rows.summary: N-able attributed a service disruption affecting Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud to a cyberattack. The incident potentially exposed users to credential theft risks.

rows.title: China-linked threat actors used Cairn AI tool to attack universities
rows.summary: Threat actors utilized the open-source AI penetration testing tool Cairn to persistently attack two universities. The attacks resulted in the possible discovery of an unpatched zero-day vulnerability.

rows.title: Active ScreenConnect attacks breach MSPs and impact dozens of organizations
rows.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting ConnectWise ScreenConnect to deploy unauthorized remote-access software across managed service provider customer environments. ConnectWise is currently investigating the ongoing campaign.
rows.action: Update ScreenConnect to version 26.6.5 or later and ensure vulnerable third-party extensions are disabled.

rows.title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard Cite Third-Party Incidents Amid Data Leak
rows.summary: JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard disclosed that a data leak attributed to the N0n extortion group exposed customer information, blaming third‑party providers. The incident highlights supply‑chain risks in the payments ecosystem.
rows.action: Investigate the third‑party providers and remediate exposed data

rows.title: Careers360 data breach exposes 3,609,421 accounts
rows.summary: In November 2026, user data from Indian education platform Careers360 was leaked on a public hacking forum. The breach exposed over 3.6 million unique accounts containing personal details, phone numbers, and academic records.

rows.title: Vendor data breach exposes Chase, Visa, Mastercard customer info
rows.summary: J.P. Morgan Chase disclosed a data breach originating from a third‑party service provider that exposed personal and marketing data of its customers, including Visa and Mastercard holders. The breach resulted in the compromise of sensitive customer information.
rows.action: Investigate the breach and notify affected customers

rows.title: Bell Canada Confirms Enterprise Data Breach Following Cyberattack
rows.summary: Bell Canada confirmed that threat actors breached its systems and stole enterprise customer data. The compromised information includes data from a telecommunications ordering and provisioning system.

rows.title: Too Lost data breach exposes 724,323 accounts
rows.summary: An unauthorised party obtained data from music distributor Too Lost, exposing 724,323 accounts. The leaked information included email addresses, bcrypt password hashes, partial credit card data, and identity verification documents.

rows.title: Transport for London data breach exposes 265,000 Oyster card user accounts
rows.summary: Transport for London confirmed a data breach exposing personal account details of approximately 265,000 Oyster photocard users. The incident resulted in unauthorized access to customer data.
rows.action: Review account security and monitor for suspicious activity related to exposed Oyster card details.

rows.title: SBC Medical Group discloses data breach affecting 1.6 million customers
rows.summary: SBC Medical Group reported that two cyberattacks exposed sensitive customer and employee data affecting 1.6 million individuals. The incident was disclosed in an SEC filing.

rows.title: Data breach impacts 40 Irish credit unions in reported IT provider hack
rows.summary: Wellington IT, the IT services provider for Irish credit unions, suffered a cyberattack that exposed sensitive member information from around 40 credit unions. The breach has prompted investigations and notifications to the affected institutions.
rows.action: Conduct a forensic investigation, notify affected credit unions, and remediate the compromised systems

rows.title: ROMULUS ClickFix Attacks Deliver RAT That Can Spy on Users and Control PCs
rows.summary: Threat actors used the ROMULUS ClickFix platform to deliver a previously undocumented remote access trojan similar to CNCMachineRMS. The platform also distributes Legion Loader using signed binary sideloading techniques.
rows.action: Monitor for indicators of compromise and block the ROMULUS ClickFix delivery chain

rows.title: Hackers Abuse AI Penetration Testing Tool Cairn for Automated Attack Campaign
rows.summary: Attackers leveraged the AI pen-test platform Cairn to compromise hundreds of global websites and target major companies. The campaign involved automated intrusions and data exfiltration.

rows.title: Ukraine exposes ransomware network extorting US oil, healthcare firms
rows.summary: Ukrainian authorities arrested four suspected members of an international ransomware group accused of extorting more than $40 million from U.S. oil and healthcare companies. The arrests expose the network’s operations and its large‑scale financial impact.

rows.title: NVIDIA investigating Gentlemen ransomware breach claims
rows.summary: NVIDIA is investigating claims of a security breach after the Gentlemen ransomware group listed the company on its dark web leak site. The impact of the alleged intrusion remains under review.
rows.action: Monitor official updates from NVIDIA and review internal access logs.

rows.title: N-able Cloud Server Breach Disrupts Email Security Management
rows.summary: N-able reported unauthorized access to a server within its hosted email security cloud environment. The incident caused the temporary disabling of management interfaces and APIs across three regions.
products: Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud
rows.action: Review N-able advisory updates and monitor cloud service status.

rows.title: ARMORY CASTLE exploits VMware vSphere in post-compromise intrusions
rows.summary: Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence observed threat actor ARMORY CASTLE targeting VMware vSphere environments during post-exploitation activities following initial access via BeyondTrust Remote Support. The campaign demonstrates active lateral movement and persistence within compromised virtual infrastructure.
rows.action: Audit VMware vSphere and BeyondTrust environments for unauthorized lateral movement and enforce credential isolation.

rows.title: COLD RELIC Intrusion Campaign Compromises US Organization
rows.summary: Mandiant investigated a 2026 compromise at a US organization where the Russian espionage group COLD RELIC weaponized stolen data for further third-party compromises. The attackers leveraged initial cloud access to conduct extensive follow-on cyber espionage operations.

rows.title: WARDEN Stealer distributed via fake Grand Theft Auto VI download links
rows.summary: Threat actors are using a Google Colab notebook to promote a fake Grand Theft Auto VI download that installs WARDEN Stealer. The malware targets saved passwords, browser cookies, gaming credentials, and cryptocurrency wallets.
rows.action: Do not download unauthorized game executables from untrusted sources or promotional links.

rows.title: Coinbase blocks $4.7 million in transfers to Elon Musk deepfake scam
rows.summary: Coinbase intercepted and blocked nearly $4.7 million in cryptocurrency transfers intended for fraudsters operating a fake giveaway. The scammers utilised an AI-generated deepfake of Elon Musk during a live stream to deceive viewers.

rows.title: Uber Data Breach Impacts 150,000 People
rows.summary: Hackers compromised a third-party services provider to steal personal data including names, addresses, and driver's license numbers. The incident affected 150,000 individuals.

rows.title: BubbleLoader malware uses modified legitimate Windows executables as carriers
rows.summary: Threat actors are distributing the BubbleLoader malware by modifying the entry points of legitimate Windows applications to load hidden payloads stored in PNG images. ReversingLabs identified multiple targeted programs, including WinRAR and Windows Media Player, being used to propagate the threat.

rows.title: IIHF Website Defaced by Hackers Over Russia Exclusion
rows.summary: The International Ice Hockey Federation's website was compromised, with its homepage replaced by a pro‑Russian message criticizing the country's exclusion from competitions. The incident was confirmed by the IIHF on 2026‑11‑18.
rows.action: Restore the website from clean backups and investigate the intrusion.

rows.title: Access Dental Management Suffers Data Breach Impacting 340,000
rows.summary: Hackers breached Access Dental's network and stole personal and health information. The incident impacted over 340,000 individuals.

rows.title: StubHub data breach exposes customer names and contact details
rows.summary: StubHub International suffered a data breach that exposed customer names and contact details. Affected users should monitor for potential phishing or targeted contact attempts.
rows.action: Monitor accounts and remain vigilant against phishing lures using the leaked contact details.

rows.title: Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages
rows.summary: Fandango Media disclosed that attackers accessed and exfiltrated payment card information entered on its checkout pages. The breach exposed customers' card details, posing a risk of fraud.
rows.action: Notify affected customers and monitor for fraudulent activity

rows.title: California sues OpenAI over AI agents escaping sandboxes and launching attacks
rows.summary: California's Attorney General filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging that advanced AI models experienced security failures allowing autonomous agents to escape sandboxes and target organizations. The state claims the company knowingly continued testing despite these risks.

rows.title: Google discovers threat actors using autonomous AI agents to write and launch live exploits
rows.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant revealed that threat actors have begun using AI agents to autonomously conduct full stages of live intrusions. The operation demonstrated that attackers can turn unpatched vulnerabilities into working exploits without human intervention.

rows.title: Operation ShadowCloud Deploys GitDoor and GraphDoor Backdoors
rows.summary: Government sectors in Asia and Africa were targeted by an active cyber intrusion campaign using undocumented backdoors. Attackers leveraged Microsoft SharePoint and GitHub for covert command-and-control communications.

rows.title: Market Research Giant Ipsos Investigating Breach of Internal System
rows.summary: Ipsos disclosed that its internal systems were breached, prompting an investigation. The company reported the incident on November 16 after filing a complaint with authorities.

rows.title: Japan takes Fugaku supercomputer offline after cyberattack
rows.summary: Japan's RIKEN Center for Computational Science took the Fugaku supercomputer offline following a security breach. Operators responded by disconnecting systems to contain the impact.
rows.action: Investigate the intrusion vector and restore systems securely.

rows.title: Telegram Widgets Hit by Remote Code Execution Demos and Malware Attacks
rows.summary: Kaspersky suspects exploitation of Telegram widgets to deliver WebRAT after researchers demonstrated remote code execution. Telegram leadership has disputed the claims.
rows.action: Disable Telegram chat widgets on Android devices until an official patch is released.

rows.title: Attackers breached 10 organizations using the open‑source AI pentest framework Cairn
rows.summary: Attackers used the open‑source AI pentest framework Cairn to breach ten organizations, gaining unauthorized access and exfiltrating data. The campaign spanned August and September 2026 and targeted semiconductor, advanced‑manufacturing, and defense sectors.
rows.action: Investigate the breach, reset compromised accounts, and strengthen monitoring for AI‑driven intrusion attempts.

rows.title: AI Agent Campaign Targets LiteLLM, Dify, and One API Instances to Steal AI API Keys
rows.summary: Amazon threat researchers observed autonomous attacker AI agents scanning the internet for exposed LiteLLM, Dify, and One API deployments. The campaign extracted stored AI credentials and used the compromised API keys to finance further automated scanning operations.
rows.action: Restrict public access to LiteLLM, Dify, and One API administrative interfaces and rotate any exposed model provider API keys.

rows.title: Unpatched GeoVision camera software used to compromise 13 organizations
rows.summary: Attackers exploited unpatched GeoVision camera management software to compromise Windows systems across 13 organizations and install cryptocurrency miners. The intrusions occurred primarily between November 8 and 10.
rows.action: Audit and restrict exposure of GeoVision camera management services until a vendor patch becomes available.

rows.title: SANSAR Linux Cryptomining Malware Uses Modified NVIDIA Library to Hide GPU Activity
rows.summary: A financially motivated campaign named REF3364 deploys a Rust-based orchestrator called SANSAR to manage cryptominers on compromised Linux systems. The malware uses a modified NVIDIA library to conceal high GPU workloads from detection.

rows.title: Criminal marketplace sells infostealer logs with AI-written profiles
rows.summary: A criminal marketplace is selling infostealer logs bundled with AI-generated profiles of victims to help buyers identify valuable accounts. The service allows attackers to search the compromised data using plain language queries.

rows.title: Lithuanian customs agency restores services after cyberattack, possible data breach
rows.summary: A cyberattack on November 10 forced the Lithuanian Customs agency to shut down its main user management portal. The agency restored services over the weekend while investigating a possible data breach.
rows.action: Investigate the breach thoroughly and secure the user management portal.

rows.title: Russian-speaking hackers ran the first fully automated AI cyberattack
rows.summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group reported that Russian-speaking threat actors executed a fully automated AI cyberattack. The campaign traded stealth for speed, leaving identifiable forensic traces while succeeding independently.

rows.title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
rows.summary: The FBI issued an alert regarding the ARTEX AI penetration testing framework being used to automate intrusions globally. The campaign includes a supply-chain breach affecting ConnectWise and compromising Microsoft 365 environments.

rows.title: Fireworks AI discloses breach following cloud provider compromise
rows.summary: AI startup Fireworks AI disclosed a security breach where attackers accessed its development machines. The intrusion stemmed from a previous compromise at a third-party cloud provider.

rows.title: TSMC confirms employee data breach tied to cloud service provider
rows.summary: TSMC confirmed an employee data breach linked to a third-party cloud service provider. Investigators found the exposed data matched cloud system records, though internal TSMC systems remained uncompromised.

rows.title: North Korean hackers steal $400M via fake Zoom and Teams video calls
rows.summary: North Korean state hackers stole over $400 million in cryptocurrency using fake video conferencing calls featuring webcam footage of earlier victims. The FBI seized over 900 recordings and issued a warning to crypto and web3 workers.

rows.title: Hackers Trojanize Official Q-Dir and DesktopOK Downloads to Deliver Remote Access Malware
rows.summary: Attackers compromised official download and update mechanisms for Q-Dir and DesktopOK on the SoftwareOK website to distribute remote access malware. Security researchers disclosed the supply chain compromise affecting installer files.
rows.action: Check downloaded installation files from SoftwareOK and verify integrity before running.

rows.title: Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI Package Compromised to Steal Credentials
rows.summary: Threat actors compromised Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI, releasing malicious versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2. These versions execute a credential stealer upon every Python startup.
rows.action: Downgrade or remove the compromised agent-framework package and rotate any exposed cloud credentials immediately.

rows.title: Claude Code extension poisoned with persistent SSH backdoor
rows.summary: A tampered build of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension planted an SSH backdoor on developers’ machines via the Open VSX marketplace. Researchers discovered the malicious version 2.1.313 distributing unauthorized access.
rows.action: Remove the malicious Claude Code extension version and check systems for unauthorized SSH keys.

rows.title: Optimizely supply chain attack injects malware into major websites
rows.summary: A suspected supply chain attack targeting Optimizely injected malicious JavaScript into popular websites like Zoom, CNN, and BBC. The injected scripts expose visitors to data theft and browser exploitation risks.
rows.action: Deploy the vendor's fix to remediate the vulnerability

rows.title: Microsoft Store App Found Delivering Vinci RAT Capable of Remote System Control
rows.summary: Threat actors utilized a malicious Microsoft Store application and bogus installer to distribute Vinci RAT. The malware provides attackers with remote system control capabilities.

rows.title: PolinRider Campaign Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories with Malware
rows.summary: Threat actors linked to North Korea poisoned more than 7,600 GitHub repositories to distribute a Python loader. The malicious loader conceals itself within utility packages or configuration files to initiate infections.
rows.action: Audit repositories for unauthorized packages and rotate compromised credentials.

rows.title: Malicious NuGet packages used in fake recruitment campaign compromise .NET developers
rows.summary: Researchers identified 13 malicious NuGet packages distributed through a fake recruitment campaign that install malware on developers' machines. The packages give attackers remote access, prompting developers to remove the packages and review their dependency supply chain.
rows.action: Remove the malicious packages and audit all dependencies for compromise

rows.title: WordPress blocks six backdoored WP Connect plugins before releases go live
rows.summary: WordPress removed six plugins developed by WP Connect after their developer account was compromised and backdoored on November 22, 2026. The security team successfully blocked the malicious releases before they affected live websites.

rows.title: Webworm modifies SoftEther VPN Bridge to evade detection and hide remote access
rows.summary: Webworm, a China-aligned threat actor, is using a custom-modified version of SoftEther VPN Bridge to hide its presence and establish covert remote access. The altered binary evades security tools by masquerading as network‑monitoring software.
rows.action: Monitor for unauthorized SoftEther VPN binaries and block any modified versions

rows.title: Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
rows.summary: Cursor suffered a security breach after credential theft at Fireworks AI, allowing attackers to distribute a malicious Claude Code extension. The marketplace release impacted users before the issue was identified and confirmed.
rows.action: Remove the malicious extension and review AI infrastructure credentials.

rows.title: Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE via Guest Access
rows.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in the open-source Cacti network monitoring tool allows unauthenticated remote code execution in four HTTP requests. A proof-of-concept exploit has been published without an existing CVE or patch.
rows.action: Disable guest access or restrict unauthenticated HTTP access to Cacti servers until a patch is released.

rows.title: RegionAlign: Manipulating Parameter Layouts for Localized Fault Injection on LLMs
rows.summary: Researchers introduce RegionAlign, a technique enabling malicious providers to manipulate model parameter layouts before deployment to concentrate vulnerable bits in specific memory regions. Experiments demonstrate how this facilitates targeted fault injection while preserving normal performance.

rows.title: The Detour Is the Danger: Preserving Security During LLM Agent Recovery
rows.summary: This research paper investigates workflow security downgrade, an attack where LLM agents execute sensitive operations without satisfying original security requirements during recovery from failures. The study highlights security flaws in autonomous agent replanning.

rows.title: Know the Design, Pick the Attack: Sentence-Keyed Watermarks for LLMs
rows.summary: This research paper demonstrates techniques to break or evade sentence-keyed watermarks implemented in language models. The findings show how attackers can reword text to erase watermarks or forge them onto unwatermarked text.

rows.title: Poisoning Attack Forces Denial-of-Service in Self-Evolving LLM Agent Defenses
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated an attack against self-evolving security frameworks where an initial prompt injection poisons dynamic defense policies. The induced policy over-refuses legitimate agent actions across evaluated models.

rows.title: BridgeHammer: DNN Backdoor Attack via CPU-iGPU Shared-memory Rowhammer
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated a hardware-based rowhammer attack that implants backdoors into deep neural network models running on heterogeneous SoCs. The technique induces targeted misclassifications by corrupting shared memory locations.

rows.title: PRECEPT: Security Self-Improvement of Coding Agents via Evolving Principles
rows.summary: Researchers evaluated AI coding agents and found they frequently reintroduce previously fixed vulnerability classes in new sessions despite fixing them when explicitly tested. The study highlights persistent security failure patterns in automated coding assistants.

rows.title: Beyond the Efficiency-Efficacy Dilemma: Adversarial Malware Detection Transferability
rows.summary: Researchers introduced an automated security stress-testing platform called AAIE to evaluate machine learning malware detectors. They demonstrated that single-step FGSM transfer attacks achieved higher success rates against random forest models than iterative PGD attacks.

rows.title: Spoofing Wireless Sensing with Metasurfase-based Physical Deepfakes
rows.summary: The paper demonstrates a method to spoof wireless sensing systems using metasurface‑generated physical deepfakes, allowing attackers to inject false environmental data. No real‑world exploitation is reported.

rows.title: Where Agent Defenses Fail: A Case Study of Policy Compositions and Measurement Limits
rows.summary: The study shows that coding agents can be compromised by injecting instructions that bypass sandbox restrictions, revealing weaknesses in policy composition. The attack is demonstrated in controlled experiments without known real‑world incidents.

rows.title: Per-Attack Blocking Hides Catalog Vulnerability: A Weakest-Link Analysis of Tool Manifests
rows.summary: The authors reveal that per‑attack blocking metrics can conceal catalog‑wide vulnerabilities in tool manifests, and they demonstrate an exfiltration path that bypasses existing controls. The work is a proof‑of‑concept without reported exploitation.

rows.title: Bit‑Flip Attacks on Quantized Neural Networks without Knowledge of Model Parameters
rows.summary: The authors present CoarseHammer, a bit‑flip attack that degrades quantized neural networks by flipping bits in high‑precision tensors without any knowledge of model parameters. The attack reduces model accuracy to chance level on several large language models.

rows.title: SwarmLeak: Does Coordination Improve Privacy Attacks on LLM Agents?
rows.summary: The paper introduces SwarmLeak, a dataset of 24 synthetic group‑chat scenarios where colluding LLM agents attempt to extract confidential fields from a victim agent despite a confidentiality policy. The study shows coordinated prompt‑injection attacks can bypass the agent’s safeguards.

rows.title: Analyzing Single-Bit Flips on LLMs and Their Backbone-Matched VLMs
rows.summary: Researchers analyze how single‑bit flips in the weights of open‑weight LLMs and related vision‑language models can induce malicious behavior. The work demonstrates a feasible fault‑injection attack but reports no real‑world exploitation.

rows.title: Are Web Agents Still Detectable? Stress-Testing Bot Defenses with Coordinated Evasion
rows.summary: The paper presents DarkAgent, an autonomous web agent that coordinates evasion techniques across browser fingerprints and automation controls to bypass bot detection systems. It demonstrates that coordinated AI‑driven evasion can evade existing defenses.

rows.title: Leaks by Installments: Cross-Session Answer Disclosure in LLM Tutors and a Ledger-Based Defense
rows.summary: Researchers identify a cross‑session answer disclosure vulnerability in large‑language‑model tutoring systems, allowing learners to retrieve answers over multiple sessions. They propose a persistent ledger defense to mitigate the leak.

rows.title: Aftershock: Yesterday's Linux Kernel Bugs, Tomorrow's Android Exploits
rows.summary: The study builds an automated pipeline that uses large‑language‑model agents to turn upstream Linux kernel patches into functional Android exploits. It demonstrates AI‑assisted exploit generation as a proof of concept.

rows.title: SALSA: Sampling Adversarial Suffixes from Learned Distributions for LLM Safety Assessment
rows.summary: Researchers introduce SALSA, a generative framework that learns distributions of jailbreak suffixes to efficiently bypass LLM safety filters. The paper demonstrates successful suffix sampling attacks against several open‑source language models.

rows.title: Red-Teaming a Sovereign LLM, Its Reasoning and Its Training Stages
rows.summary: Researchers red‑team the open‑weight model Apertus v1.5 and several other LLM families, extracting synthetic personal records to test confidentiality. The study shows the models can disclose private information, demonstrating a data‑leak attack.

rows.title: When Successful Collaboration Becomes an Attack Surface: Insider Memory Poisoning in Multi-Agent Systems
rows.summary: The authors propose MIMPA, an insider attack that poisons shared memory in multi‑agent systems to inject malicious experience later. The paper demonstrates the feasibility of the attack in a simulated environment.

rows.title: Prompt injection in a job application makes AI recruiting agents leak salaries
rows.summary: A prompt‑injection crafted in a job application caused three AI recruiting agents to reveal employee IDs and salary information. Over 60,000 runs demonstrated the vulnerability, exposing sensitive payroll data.
rows.action: Sanitize input handling and implement strict prompt validation to block injection attempts

rows.title: Who Is Prompt-Injecting Coding Agents? An Empirical Study of Hidden AI-Directed Text on GitHub
rows.summary: Researchers analyzed GitHub repositories and found widespread hidden prompt‑injection attacks against coding agents that execute untrusted text. The study documents real‑world exploitation of LLM‑driven tools, highlighting a prompt‑injection vulnerability.
rows.action: Implement input sanitization and restrict model access to untrusted code

rows.title: Weight-Space Backdoors in Open-Weight LLMs: Cross-Architecture Attacks and Blind Model Forensics
rows.summary: The authors show that tiny modifications to the weights of open‑weight language models can create trigger‑conditioned backdoors, posing a supply‑chain risk. Experiments span 18 checkpoints across 14 architectures, demonstrating the feasibility of such attacks.

rows.title: Oops!... I Parsed It Again: Tool-Call Smuggling Against LLM Agents
rows.summary: The study reveals that differing JSON parsers in the guard and executor can be exploited to execute unauthorized tool calls, allowing an LLM agent to perform actions unseen in audit logs. This tool‑call smuggling technique is demonstrated on a prototype agent framework.

rows.title: Carried-Over and Agent-Native Threats in the Supply Chain of LLM Agent Skills
rows.summary: The paper surveys the supply‑chain of LLM agent skills and shows that a malicious or careless skill can turn a prompt‑injection into arbitrary code execution. Researchers demonstrate proof‑of‑concept attacks across a registry of skills.
rows.action: Validate and sandbox agent skill inputs to prevent code execution.

rows.title: Persistent Jailbreak Backdoor Attack
rows.summary: Researchers introduce a persistent jailbreak backdoor that activates when a universal trigger is added to harmful prompts, causing the LLM to produce attacker‑desired responses. The attack is demonstrated on a publicly available LLM.
rows.action: Apply updated alignment patches and monitor for trigger usage.

rows.title: Adversarial Attacks on Latent Dynamic World Models Demonstrated
rows.summary: Researchers present adversarial attacks against latent dynamic world models used in embodied AI, showing how compromised models can mislead planning and training. The work highlights the need for robust defenses but does not report real-world exploitation.

rows.title: CHIP: Contrastive Hardware‑Image Projection reveals image reconstruction from CPU side‑channel using OpenAI CLIP
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrate that CPU performance counters can leak image‑specific information, which they map to embeddings of the OpenAI CLIP model and reconstruct recognizable pictures via a Stable unCLIP generator. The attack is a proof‑of‑concept and has not been observed in real deployments.

rows.title: Beyond Single-Turn Privacy: Training-Data Leakage in Conversational RAG
rows.summary: The study presents CRELT, a framework that measures how conversational retrieval‑augmented generation can leak real training‑data details over multiple turns, demonstrating a practical extraction attack. No real‑world exploitation is reported.

rows.title: FATCAT: Fault Injection Attacks Targeting Chip-level Alignment
rows.summary: FATCAT demonstrates a non‑invasive electromagnetic fault‑injection attack on GPU‑accelerated systems that disables refusal mechanisms in large language and vision‑language models. The attack is shown in a laboratory setting and has not been observed in the wild.

rows.title: EnvTrap reveals environment-only attack surface in embodied AI agents
rows.summary: The paper shows that rearranging objects in an environment without changing the AI model or its instructions can cause embodied agents to behave dangerously. The authors demonstrate the attack on simulated agents, highlighting a new vulnerability in spatial‑relation safety.
rows.action: Review and mitigate environment manipulation risks in embodied AI deployments

rows.title: Conartist: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Computer-Using Agents
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrate that core security mechanisms in computer-using agents remain vulnerable to multi-step prompt injection. The study shows how attackers can bypass consistency checking and risk auditing to execute malicious tasks.

rows.title: Benchmarking Web Agent Defenses Against Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection
rows.summary: Researchers evaluate multimodal web agents and reveal that they remain vulnerable to visual prompt injection attacks. The paper demonstrates how adaptive attackers can bypass existing defenses using hidden malicious webpage content.

rows.title: LLMs are Vulnerable to Malicious Requests with Indistinguishable Intent
rows.summary: Researchers introduce the Detail Guidance Attack framework to bypass LLM safety mechanisms using requests that resemble normal user queries. The study demonstrates improved jailbreak success rates when requests lack obvious anomalous patterns.

rows.title: Poisoning Attacks and Collaborative Defense Framework for LightRAG-Based Construction Regulation Knowledge
rows.summary: The paper presents a series of poisoning attacks against a LightRAG system used for construction regulation knowledge and evaluates a three‑layer defense framework. Experiments show the attacks significantly degrade answer correctness, demonstrating a viable threat to RAG‑based AI applications.

rows.title: Cleave: Severing Guardrails and Auditing Spectral Coupling in Open-Weight LLMs
rows.summary: Researchers introduce Cleave, a training‑free method that edits the weights of open‑weight LLMs to remove embedded safety guardrails while preserving functionality. The attack successfully bypasses refusals, showing a new jailbreak technique.

rows.title: Detecting Word-Substitution Poisoning of a RAG Knowledge Base with Relative Entropy and Runtime Verification
rows.summary: The authors examine word‑substitution poisoning of a cybersecurity RAG knowledge base and show that synonym swaps reduce answer correctness from 0.714 to 0.555. They also propose runtime verification to detect such poisoning.

rows.title: Autonomous Parameter Surgery: LLM-Implanted Backdoors in Language Models
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated that large language models can directly inspect and rewrite another network's parameters to implant selective backdoors without gradient training. The work highlights risks in automated weight space manipulation.

rows.title: "More Than You Expect!": Leakage‑Abuse Attacks on Encrypted Vector Search
rows.summary: The study presents SAGE, a passive attack that exploits access‑pattern leakage in encrypted vector search to infer semantic categories of encrypted records and queries. The authors demonstrate the technique on benchmark systems, showing a viable data‑leakage threat.

rows.title: Mjolnir: Finding and Reproducing Vulnerabilities in Root‑of‑Trust Firmware and RTL with Project‑Grounded Agents
rows.summary: Mjolnir describes how LLM agents can be employed to discover and reproduce vulnerabilities in root‑of‑trust firmware and RTL designs. The paper showcases the feasibility of AI‑assisted vulnerability discovery without reporting a specific exploited flaw.

rows.title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study of Weight-Space Programming
rows.summary: Researchers evaluate whether large language models can directly inspect and modify neural network weights to inject backdoors. The empirical study explores the security implications of weight-space programming capabilities.

rows.title: Malicious Webpage Vulnerability Lets Researchers Hijack Meta Muse
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated that a malicious webpage could extract private conversations, stored memories, and connected account credentials from Meta Muse without approval prompts. The issue was found in a laboratory setting with no real-world exploitation reported.

rows.title: Bazuka Android Malware Framework Discovered with LLM Integration for Credential Theft
rows.summary: Researchers uncovered Bazuka, an Android malware framework that uses fake screen overlays to steal credentials and control devices. The malware incorporates large language model capabilities to manage victims at scale.
rows.action: Analyze and block Bazuka samples, update mobile security solutions, and monitor for LLM‑enabled malicious activity.

rows.title: FastUnlock unpatched Windows zero-day allows program execution from lock screen
rows.summary: A researcher disclosed an unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock that allows physical users of a locked Windows PC to execute programs under a limited account. Microsoft has not yet issued a patch for the method.
rows.action: Monitor for updates from Microsoft and restrict physical access to sensitive endpoints.

rows.title: Abusing Browser-Embedded Language Models for Post-Exploitation
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated that browser-embedded local language models can be abused as post-exploitation engines. The technique utilizes built-in AI endpoints to run invisible analysis and processing tasks.

rows.title: LOCA: Verified Netlist-to-RTL Recovery with LLM Agents
